title: Unique words in a sentence
description:
_I am a teacher and I love to inspire and teach people._ How many unique words have been used in the sentence? Use the split methods and set to get the unique words.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `count_unique_words(sentence)`, returning the number of unique whitespace-separated words in the given sentence.
examples: count_unique_words('I am a teacher and I love to inspire and teach people.') -> 10
hints: First break the sentence into individual words, the same way you'd tokenize any string on whitespace.
Once you have a list of words, feed it into a set to collapse any words that appear more than once.
Use sentence.split() to get the words, wrap the result in set(...), and return its len().
expected_behavior: Splits the sentence on whitespace into words, then returns the count of distinct words (case-sensitive, punctuation attached to a word counts as part of that word).

hidden_tests.call: count_unique_words('I am a teacher and I love to inspire and teach people.')
hidden_tests.label: original sentence, 'I' and 'and' each repeat once

hidden_tests.call: count_unique_words('the quick brown fox the lazy dog')
hidden_tests.label: sentence with one repeated word

explanation: str.split() with no arguments breaks the string on whitespace into a list of words. Wrapping that list in set(...) collapses any repeated words into one, so len() of the resulting set gives the count of distinct words.
